title: ALMA/NICER observations of GRS 1915+105 indicate a return to a hard state
question: Study the jet and accretion disk properties of GRS 1915+105 during its 2018-2019 outburst decay to determine if it has descended into a low-luminosity hard X-ray state.

what.value: 350 GHz JCMT observations of GRS 1915+105 during a radio-quiet state

evidence.quote: We used the 350 GHz James Clerk Maxwell Telescope (JCMT) observations from Ogley et al. (2000) that were taken during a radio-quiet state

what.value: 94 GHz Nobeyama Millimeter Array (NMA) observations of GRS 1915+105 during a radio plateau state

evidence.quote: and 94 GHz Nobeyama Millimeter Array (NMA) observations from Ueda et al. (2002) that were taken during a radio plateau state, both of which should present a compact steady jet.

what.value: GX 339-4 hard-state 8.4 GHz radio and 3-10 keV X-ray correlation data

evidence.quote: For comparison, we plotted the GX 339-4 hard-state radio/X-ray correlation (gray triangles; same X-ray band, but radio luminosity is from 8.4 GHz; from Koljonen & Russell 2019).

recipe.goal: Calibrate, flag, and extract flux densities and polarization from ALMA Band 3 data
recipe.method: Run provided ALMA calibration script in CASA, apply manual channel and antenna flags for bad D-terms and gain/phase outliers, image the data, and fit a delta function to the uv-plane using uvmultifit to measure Stokes I, Q, U fluxes (full band, per spectral window, and per scan).
key_parameters: Flagged first 10 channels in spw 2 (both epochs); flagged DA63 (Epoch 1) and DA41 (Epoch 2) all spws; flagged DA42 and DA48 spw 1 (Epoch 2)
Scan length ~10 min for intra-epoch timing
assumptions: Point source model (delta function in uv-plane)

recipe.goal: Reduce NICER X-ray observations and model Power Spectral Densities (PSDs) and QPO lags
recipe.method: Filter NICER events using nicerdas, calculate rms-normalized PSDs in 1-10 keV, fit PSDs in ISIS with up to three Lorentzians plus power-law and constant Poisson noise, and compute time lags between 2-4 keV and 5-10 keV bands.
key_parameters: nicercal_filtexpr="EVENT_FLAGS=bx1x000", cor_range="4-", PI channels 30-1200 (0.3-12 keV), exposure > 500 s
PSD binning 2^-7 s (or 2^-4 s in obscured phase), segment length 16 s (or 256 s in obscured phase), geometric rebinning factor 1.05
assumptions: Poisson noise is constant power component

recipe.goal: Fit NICER X-ray energy spectra and iron line evolution across outburst decay phases
recipe.method: Adaptively bin NICER spectra (0.3-12 keV) by S/N and fit in ISIS with vphabs * (relxill + lines) + powerlaw (adding xillver in the obscured phase) to extract continuum parameters, fluxes, and iron absorption/emission line properties.
key_parameters: Adaptive binning: 0.3-1.5 keV to S/N=5-10, 1.5-5.0 keV to S/N=20-70, 5.0-8.0 keV to S/N=15-50, 8.0-12.0 keV to S/N=10-30
Obscured phase: R_in = 1, R_f = -2, inclination free
assumptions: Black hole spin a = 0, inclination i = 70 deg (except obscured phase), solar iron abundance

recipe.goal: Evaluate the millimeter/X-ray luminosity correlation and fit the X-ray light curve decay profile
recipe.method: Combine ALMA Band 3 luminosities and NICER 3-10 keV luminosities with archival JCMT/NMA and RXTE data to fit the mm/X-ray correlation slope, and fit the NICER 1-10 keV light curve with an exponential-to-linear decay model.
assumptions: Distance d = 8.6 kpc, black hole mass M = 12 M_sun, Eddington luminosity L_Edd = 1.5 x 10^39 erg s^-1, flat radio/mm spectrum

score_reason: ALMA data reduction, antenna/channel flagging, and uvmultifit modeling are clearly specified with exact software versions, and NICER timing/spectral parameters and full fit tables are provided, with only minor imaging parameters and exact archival X-ray ObsIDs omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Both the ALMA (2018.1.00621.S) and NICER (HEASARC) datasets are public, the uv-plane point-source fitting and X-ray spectral/timing recipes are well-specified, and all key results (Stokes I/Q/U fluxes, spectral indices, polarization fractions, decay timescales, and mm/X-ray slope) are numeric.
